questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to parked vehicles to give more room to moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians go, then go.
Slow down and go carefully.
Stop completely and wait until the light is no longer red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians go, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a full stop, then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop Sign Ahead.
Side Road.
Railroad Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they cannot show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to drive with if you don't feel sleepy.
Over-the-counter drugs can also affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can also affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can harm your driving, including cold medicine, allergy pills, and muscle relaxers. It is illegal to drive while any drug affects your driving ability. The law applies to illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter drugs equally.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must always be given the right-of-way.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual spot, you should:

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from any direction.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from any direction.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked vehicle does not become a hazard. Park where drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look to both sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to both sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross your path or traffic lines meet, look left and right to make sure no one is coming.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming vehicle has high beams on and blinds you. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. You do not have to stop completely.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert and careful. Slow down and watch for other traffic.

questions.question: It is illegal to park:

options.text: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. You also cannot park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see and be seen. The best way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn on:

options.text: Your dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Use low beam headlights if you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before going.
Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
Keep your speed steady and look for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic on the road you want to enter or cross go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop. Let any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians pass before you go. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: A DUI conviction is based on a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
50 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent or higher. Drivers under 21 face penalties for levels as low as 0.02 percent. You can be convicted of DUI even with a lower blood alcohol level.

questions.question: If you want to enter the freeway but do not see a gap in traffic, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap. If you stop at the end of the ramp, you will not have enough space to speed up to match the traffic before entering.

questions.question: You should hold the steering wheel with both hands at:

options.text: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock.
11 o'clock and 6 o'clock.
7 o'clock and 5 o'clock.

questions.correctAnswerText: 9 o'clock and 3 o'clock.
questions.explanation: Place your left hand at 9 o'clock and your right hand at 3 o'clock on the steering wheel.

questions.question: To know where traffic is behind you, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: A U-turn is not allowed:

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You may not be able to see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a crash.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Looking at crashes while driving slows traffic and causes congestion. You should avoid doing this.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic citation.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when driving. Show your insurance proof and license to an officer whenever they ask, whether you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic violation.

questions.question: Highway driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe highway driving means you must stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds safely.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in a person's blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood. A higher BAC number means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly and check your blind spots.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly and check your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots or be missed in quick glances. Always watch for them and check your mirrors and blind spots regularly.

questions.question: You are driving on a city street and see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights and sirens. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only on rural roads when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beams when you are following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: If you see that the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and take another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and take another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may look shallow but can hide hazards. Find another route to your destination.

questions.question: Speeding too much:

options.text: Saves time so you arrive faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor driving decisions and serious crashes.
